spring:
  # No embedded fallback. Use jdbc:postgresql://... or jdbc:mysql://... .
  # The JDBC driver and Hibernate dialect are inferred from the URL.
  datasource:
    embedded-database-connection: none
    url: ${DB_URL}
    username: ${DB_USERNAME}
    password: ${DB_PASSWORD}
  jpa:
    hibernate:
      ddl-auto: validate
  liquibase:
    enabled: true
    change-log: classpath:db/changelog/db.changelog-master.yaml
  session:
    jdbc:
      initialize-schema: never
  sql:
    init:
      mode: never
  h2:
    console:
      enabled: false

server:
  forward-headers-strategy: framework
  servlet:
    session:
      cookie:
        secure: true
        http-only: true
        same-site: strict

app:
  cors:
    allowed-origins: ${APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS:}
  password-reset:
    log-reset-link: false
    # No localhost fallback — the day a real EmailService replaces the stub,
    # an unset value must not silently emit reset links pointing at
    # localhost:3000.
    link-base-url: ${APP_RESET_LINK_BASE_URL:}
  admin:
    username: ${APP_ADMIN_USERNAME:}
    password: ${APP_ADMIN_PASSWORD:}
    email: ${APP_ADMIN_EMAIL:admin@localhost}

spring:
  application:
    name: hello-auth
  datasource:
    url: jdbc:h2:mem:helloauth
    username: sa
    password: ""
  jpa:
    hibernate:
      ddl-auto: validate
  liquibase:
    change-log: classpath:db/changelog/db.changelog-master.yaml
  sql:
    init:
      mode: never
  session:
    # Spring Session JDBC over H2 — the ratified store (ticket 02). Sessions
    # persist in SPRING_SESSION, enabling true invalidation and per-user
    # session enumeration (findByPrincipalName) for later tickets.
    store-type: jdbc
    # Pinned idle timeout (security-review F-08): 30m is also the framework
    # default — set explicitly so the value survives default changes and the
    # session-lifetime contract is visible in config, not implied.
    timeout: 30m
    jdbc:
      initialize-schema: never
  mvc:
    problemdetails:
      enabled: true

server:
  port: 8080
  servlet:
    session:
      cookie:
        http-only: true
        # Set explicitly — a Boot 4.1 regression can otherwise leave SameSite
        # unset instead of Lax (spring-boot#48830). secure=true only in the
        # prod profile (hardening ticket).
        same-site: lax
        secure: false

management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health

# Externalized security tunables (ticket 06 decision).
app:
  password-min-length: 12
  # Two-layer brute-force defense (ticket 11). ip-throttle.max-failures stays
  # below lockout.max-failures so a single source IP can never record enough
  # failures to lock an account — the literal anti-DoS guarantee.
  lockout:
    max-failures: 5
    window: 10m
    cooldown: 15m
  ip-throttle:
    max-failures: 4
    # anon-max-requests (security-review F-04): per-IP budget for the
    # unauthenticated mutations (register, password-reset/request) — a
    # second, independent bucket counting every hit, sharing the window
    # and max-entries below.
    anon-max-requests: 20
    window: 10m
    max-entries: 10000
  # Single-use reset tokens (ticket 12): 32-byte SecureRandom, only the
  # SHA-256 hash is stored, lifetime inside the spec's 15–30 min bound. The
  # stubbed EmailService logs link-base-url?token=<token> — no SMTP exists.
  # cleanup-interval (ticket 14): cadence of the scheduled purge that deletes
  # consumed/expired token rows. log-reset-link (security-review F-02): the
  # link line carries the plaintext token — a live bearer credential — so
  # the prod profile sets it false and the stub logs a token-free
  # suppressed-delivery line instead.
  password-reset:
    token-ttl: 15m
    link-base-url: http://localhost:3000/reset-password
    cleanup-interval: 1h
    log-reset-link: true
  # Initial-admin bootstrap (ticket 13). Credentials come from the
  # APP_ADMIN_* env vars; blank means "not configured" and nothing is
  # seeded. The dev profile ships documented defaults; the prod profile
  # (ticket 14) requires the env vars outright so a missing config fails
  # fast rather than leaving no way into /api/admin/**.
  admin:
    username: ${APP_ADMIN_USERNAME:}
    password: ${APP_ADMIN_PASSWORD:}
    email: ${APP_ADMIN_EMAIL:admin@localhost}
  # CORS allow-list for the credentialed SPA origin(s) (ticket 14). The
  # dev/local default is the Vite origin; the prod profile binds
  # APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS (comma-separated) with a blank default —
  # an unset list permits no origins (fail-closed).
  cors:
    allowed-origins: ${APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS:http://localhost:3000}
